entity_title: Employer needs Unemployment Fund permit first
fact_text: Before a third-country national can apply to the Police and Border Guard Board for a residence permit for employment, the employer must generally first obtain a permit from the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund (Töötukassa) to fill the position with a foreign national.
evidence_quote: The employer obtains a permit from the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund to recruit a foreign national for the position.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employer can hire and sponsor the worker directly. Actually the employer must first secure a separate permit from the Unemployment Insurance Fund (Töötukassa) before the residence-permit application, a labour-market step that adds lead time. Action: have the employer obtain the Töötukassa permit before booking the residence-permit appointment.

entity_title: Salary must meet Estonian average wage
fact_text: To qualify for a residence permit for employment, the employer must pay the third-country national a salary at least equal to the Estonian average gross salary (the general requirement, subject to role-specific exceptions).
evidence_quote: The employer pays you a salary that is at least equal to the average gross salary in Estonia (general requirement, subject to exceptions).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any agreed market salary is acceptable. Actually the pay must reach at least the Estonian average gross salary, a statutory floor updated periodically. Action: confirm the offered gross salary meets or exceeds the current Estonian average wage before applying.

fact_text: A third-country national staying legally in Estonia can have their work registered as short-term employment instead of applying for a residence permit; this may cover more than 5 days within 1 month and up to 365 days within a 455-day period.
evidence_quote: more than 5 days within 1 month and up to 365 days within 455 days

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a full residence permit is the only route to start working. Actually short-term-employment registration is a faster alternative allowing up to 365 days of work within 455 days. Action: for assignments under a year, evaluate short-term employment registration instead of a residence permit.

entity_title: Short-term registration is not a right to stay
fact_text: Registering short-term employment authorises work but does not by itself grant the third-country national the right to stay in Estonia; a separate legal basis for stay, such as a visa, is still required.
evidence_quote: Registration of short-term employment does not grant the foreign national the right to stay in Estonia. To stay in Estonia, foreign nationals must apply for a visa.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed that having short-term employment registered means you are cleared to stay in Estonia. Actually the registration covers only the work; the person must separately hold a visa or other lawful basis of stay. Action: pair the short-term-employment registration with a valid visa or residence basis, never rely on it alone.

entity_title: Employer, not employee, registers short-term work
fact_text: Short-term employment in Estonia is registered by the employer with the Police and Border Guard Board; the employee does not file the registration themselves.
evidence_quote: Short-term employment is registered by your employer. You do not need to do anything yourself to register short-term employment.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the arriving worker must lodge their own work registration. Actually the employer submits the short-term-employment registration and the employee does nothing for it. Action: confirm the Estonian employer has filed the registration before the worker starts.

entity_title: Register your address after the permit
fact_text: After receiving the residence permit, the third-country national must settle in Estonia and register their place of residence (address) in the Population Register.
evidence_quote: You will settle in Estonia after receiving the residence permit and register your place of residence in the Population Register.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the residence-permit card is the last step. Actually the holder must also register their address in the Population Register after arriving, which many local services and the tax office then rely on. Action: register the Estonian address in the Population Register promptly after moving in.

entity_title: Estonian A2 exam needed to extend after 5 years
fact_text: Extending or renewing a residence permit for employment can require passing the Estonian language exam at level A2; this requirement has applied since 15 July 2018 for holders who have lived in Estonia for 5 years on such a permit.
evidence_quote: Since 15th of July 2018 the requirement of Estonian language exam level A2 has been established.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed English is enough throughout an Estonian work-permit stay. Actually extending the permit after 5 years can require an A2-level Estonian language exam pass. Action: budget time for Estonian language study well before the first extension is due.

entity_title: 183 days makes you an Estonian tax resident
fact_text: A natural person who arrives in Estonia becomes an Estonian tax resident if they stay in Estonia for at least 183 days over the course of 12 consecutive calendar months.
evidence_quote: the person is staying in Estonia for at least 183 days over the course of a period of 12 consecutive calendar months

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed tax residency follows the calendar year or the permit. Actually the test is 183 days within any 12 consecutive calendar months, so it can be triggered mid-year. Action: track days present in Estonia across a rolling 12-month window, not just the calendar year.

entity_title: Estonian tax residents are taxed worldwide
fact_text: Once a person is an Estonian tax resident, Estonia taxes their income earned both in Estonia and abroad, not only their Estonian-source income.
evidence_quote: A resident natural person must pay income tax on all income derived by him or her in Estonia and outside Estonia

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed Estonia only taxes the salary earned in Estonia. Actually once you are an Estonian tax resident, worldwide income becomes taxable in Estonia (subject to tax treaties). Action: review home-country income and any tax treaty before residency is triggered to avoid double taxation surprises.

entity_title: e-Residency is not a residence permit
fact_text: Estonia's e-Resident's digital ID lets a foreigner identify themselves and sign digitally in Estonian e-services, but it does not grant any right to reside or work in Estonia.
evidence_quote: digital ID does not grant the right to reside in Estonia.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed e-Residency is a form of Estonian residency or a shortcut to relocating. Actually the e-Resident's digital ID is only a digital identity for e-services and confers no right to reside. Action: a relocating employee still needs a residence permit or short-term-employment basis; e-Residency does not substitute for it.

entity_title: You can get an isikukood before residency
fact_text: An Estonian personal identification code (isikukood) can be granted to people who are not permanent residents but need it to have their data entered in Estonian state databases (e.g. the Tax and Customs Board, Health Insurance Fund or Social Insurance Board).
evidence_quote: A personal identification code is granted to people who are not permanent residents in Estonia

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the isikukood only comes with the residence-permit card. Actually a personal identification code can be granted to a non-permanent-resident who needs it for entry into state databases (tax, health, social insurance). Action: obtain the isikukood early so payroll, tax and health registrations are not blocked.
